basis: L187 per-module receipts (research evidence/replay-l187-20261109/batches/*/results.jsonl.xz): lean -j1 -M7000 wall per module, 14101 modules, one lean process each, exit 0
scenario_notes: overhead = per-scope launch cost not in the lean wall (systemd-run, admission checks, dependency hashing). L187 observed 30-40 s per scope launched over ssh (L187_ESTIMATE.json); a host-local runner is expected to be nearer 3-10 s; 40 s kept as the pessimistic bound. Greedy list scheduling in dependency order, longest-remaining-path priority; assumes 5 slots always granted (Stream C share and host count may allow fewer).

measured_dryrun.per_scope_overhead_s: about 3 (admission ~1 s + systemd scope start/exit ~1-2 s; first dry run showed a 30 s wait that was a runner bug (waiting for a scope that had already exited), fixed)

headline.note: expected ~4-8 h at 5 concurrent scopes (3-10 s overhead); 3 slots ~6-13 h; critical path 1.1-2.3 h. Excludes handover waiting, any failed-module repairs and the 12 h/400-scope thresholds that stopped the L187 plan (one scope per module is 10684 scopes; the lead must confirm this shape or approve a batch shape like L187 option B).

rss_caveat: L187 peak_rss_kib is the lean process max RSS from /usr/bin/time -v and includes memory-mapped olean pages. The dry-run cgroup peaks were 0.35 GB against RSS 3.3 GB, and the L187 maximum batch cgroup peak was 5.07 GB, so the cgroup caps (MemoryHigh 6G, MemoryMax 8G) were not approached; the Lean -M7000 limit (7,168,000 KiB) is the binding one. Highest L187 RSS: 7,087,904 KiB (98.9% of -M7000).
